title: ALTERNATOR SYSTEM - TROUBLESHOOTING
question: What troubleshooting steps should be taken if the low voltage light does not go out when the alternator and battery switches are turned on with the engine running?
answer: A troubleshooting chart has been developed to aid the maintenance technician in system Refer to the Lamar TE04 MCU Test Set and the LI-0021 instructions for additional testing procedures of the alternator system. Refer to Electrical Power- General, Tools, Equipment, BREAKER. REMOVE "B" LEAD FROM ALTERNATOR. TURN BATTERY AND ALTERNATOR SWITCH ON. IF ALTERNATOR FIELD CIRCUIT BREAKER. DISCONNECT ALTERNATOR POWER WIRE FROM ACU. TURN ON BATTAND ALT SWITCHES. IF ALTERNATOR BREAKER. DISCONNECT FIELD WIRE FROM FIELD TERMINAL OF ALTERNATOR. TURN BATT AND ALT SWITCH ON. IF IF NOT, FIELD IS SHORTED INSIDE IF NOT, THEN TURN OFF BATT AND ALT TURN ON BATT AND ALT SWITCH. IF ENGINE IS RUNNING. ALTERNATOR AND BATTERY SWITCH ON. WITH ENGINE RUNNING, LOW VOLTAGE LIGHT DOES NOT GO OUT WHEN ALTERNATOR AND BATTERY SWITCHES ARE TURNED ON, ALL OTHER SWITCHES OFF. CHECK BUS VOLTAGE. WITH ENGINE RUNNING, IF 25V OR HIGHER, PANEL FOR SHORT TO GROUND. IF SHORT IF NOT, THEN CHECK FIELD VOLTAGE NOT RUNNING. IF THERE IS LESS CONTACTOR. IF IT IS WITHIN 2V OF SHOULD BE THE SAME . SINCE THE ALTERNATOR HAS AN INTERNAL CAPACITOR, READINGS TAKEN WITH METERS SELECTED ON RESISTANCE MAY BE UNSTABLE. IF READINGS ARE OBTAINED THAT DIFFER FROM PREVIOUSLY STATED,
